newsitem.title: USA: Agronomist says Arkansas wheat quality looks good.
newsitem.headline: Agronomist says Arkansas wheat quality looks good.

text.p: University of Arkansas Extension Agronomist William Johnson said the quality of Arkansas's soft red winter wheat looks good but yields per acre may be lower than last year.
He also said some of the state's crop had to be destroyed early this spring because of heavy rainfall which will trim the state's total wheat production potential.
"We had late planting (last fall) and a tremendous amount of rainfall," Johnson told Reuters in an inverview overnight Tuesday. "About 100,000 acres were plowed up this spring."
Johnson noted that 790,000 acres remain available for harvest. "For 1997 (harvest) Arkansas was forecast to plant about 1.5 million acres and we got 880,000 acres planted."

He said test weights would be at about 56.60 pounds per bushel, about average. But yields were estimated at around 38 to 42 bushels per acre, down from last year's U.S. Department of Agriculture 54 bushels per acre.
Arkansas's five year average yield from 1990 to 1994 was 38.4 bushels per acre, according to USDA.
